text: What is the central disagreement between Platonic (ante rem) and Aristotelian (in re) realism about universals?
choices: Whether universals are concrete or abstract; Platonism says concrete, Aristotelianism says abstract.
Whether universals can exist uninstantiated; Platonism allows uninstantiated universals, while immanent realism holds a universal exists only in its instances.
Whether there are any universals at all; Platonists affirm them and Aristotelians deny them.
Whether resemblance among particulars is primitive; Platonists say yes, Aristotelians say no.
explanation: For Platonism, triangularity exists even if nothing is triangular; immanent realism (Aristotle, Armstrong) holds a universal exists only where instantiated. The tempting distractor (option 2) confuses this intra-realist dispute with the realism/nominalism debate, but both Platonists and Aristotelians are realists about universals.
